fields.sections.0.h: Only tech giants show performance improvement, broader companies remain stagnant
fields.sections.1.h: Over-investment by venture companies vs. skepticism from general businesses
fields.sections.2.h: Why cheaper AI technology does not necessarily lead to increased revenue
fields.sections.3.h: AI's success is determined by broad enterprises, not tech companies
fields.sections.0.ko: Despite massive investment in AI and widespread expectations, U.S. companies outside the technology sector have yet to realize substantial financial gains. While the Mag 7 (large tech stocks) are seeing increases in revenue per employee and improving profitability, the same metrics for the S&P 493 (remaining companies) show almost no change. This suggests that AI investment has not brought productivity improvements across the broader economy. Consequently, mainstream companies have begun to view AI-related spending primarily as a cost that erodes net income rather than as a source of growth.
fields.sections.1.ko: Companies receiving venture capital funding are increasingly investing larger amounts in using AI models. Conversely, mainstream companies do not need the latest models and are unwilling to pay extra for them. As long as AI-related spending remains confined to a small portion of the economy, AI's macroeconomic impact will necessarily be extremely limited. This disparity reveals a gap in perception between technology investors' optimism and the actual state of business operations.
fields.sections.2.ko: The challenge ahead is whether AI models will become increasingly cheaper while mainstream companies successfully convert their use into revenue growth and improved profitability. The key point is that this may be more difficult than expected. While AI is an excellent computational tool, what real business operations require is judgment rather than information. Judgment varies according to specific context and changes depending on who or which model makes the decision. More importantly, AI does not understand concepts such as accountability, trust, culture, unwritten rules, ethical trade-offs, and fairness. These factors determine a company's reputational risk and ultimately drive revenue growth and profit margins.
fields.sections.3.ko: In conclusion, the key metric for assessing AI's overall economic impact is not the Mag 7 but the performance of the S&P 493. Based on available data to date, there is no evidence of improved revenue growth or profitability outside the technology sector. This means that the economic effects of AI investment have not yet reached the monetization stage.
fields.caveat: This analysis represents the position of Apollo Asset Management's chief economist and is based on data from a specific point in time (the exact compilation date is not specified), so verification against the latest economic trends is needed.
